reason: Both correctly identify the run-on as a normal cooling fan and set the right escalation threshold (runs for hours or when cold), with no part recommendation and no unsafe DIY. Conversation 2 is tighter and more accurate to the situation: it links longer run-on to a hot or long cook (matching the 220C 90-minute roast), gives a clear 'leave it and see if it stops when fully cool' first step, and names an engineer as the only escalation. Conversation 1 muddles its threshold with 'hasn't stopped after several hours of being completely switched off at the wall' (a fan cannot run with mains off), which could confuse the homeowner, and it drifts toward blaming the 'fan motor' without basis.
